documents.title: AI Appropriate Use Procedure
documents.stance_why: The procedure says USU is "forward-looking" and asks "how do we enable our people to use these tools", while setting conditions (accountability, verification, data classification, a list of prohibited uses). It allows AI with conditions and sets no ban or per-course rule, so permit.
documents.summary: Procedure aimed at faculty, staff and researchers: it welcomes AI and sets principles, data rules and prohibited uses, but no coursework rule for students.

units.why: A principle binding every user: "accountable for your work product, whether AI helped create it or not", i.e. ownership of what one submits, so P29.
units.anchor: You are accountable for your work product, whether AI helped create it or not.

units.why: States the purpose and governing policy of the procedure ("procedure for appropriate AI use as required by Policy 5200"), an institution-level framework preamble, so P56.
units.anchor: documents USU's procedure for appropriate AI use as required by Policy 5200, Section 2.8

units.why: The procedure frames its default as enabling rather than restricting ("not how do we restrict this"), a permit/encourage-by-default stance for employees, so P02.
units.anchor: how do we enable our people to use these tools effectively, confidently, responsibly

units.why: Sets the scope of the principles ("any AI tool, any workflow, and any role"); a scope/principles statement fits P56 better than P61 since it defines coverage not terms.
units.anchor: They apply to any AI tool, any workflow, and any role at USU

units.why: Tells users to "review AI-generated work for accuracy, bias" before using it in academic contexts, i.e. verify output because it is often wrong: P31.
units.anchor: Review AI-generated work for accuracy, bias, and copyright compliance before using it

units.why: Asks users to consider data "risk classification" before putting university information into an AI tool, a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: consider its risk classification

units.why: Gives a conservative default for data classification ("treat data at the highest applicable tier"), still P50 personal-data protection.
units.anchor: when in doubt, treat data at the highest applicable tier

units.why: "critical thinking, academic rigor, and professional judgment remain yours": the human stays the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: AI supports your judgment; it does not replace it.

units.why: Directs users to "disclose AI use where it is expected or required" including academic work: a disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: Disclose AI use where it is expected or required

units.why: Defers disclosure rules to the journal, funder or department, which P62 names ("deferring to venue, funder" rules).
units.anchor: Follow your department's, journal's, or funding agency's disclosure guidance.
units.fit_note: Also defers to the department, not only venue or funder.

units.why: "Be thoughtful about copyright and licensing" is the P52 concern with IP of AI output.
units.anchor: Be thoughtful about copyright and licensing when using AI

units.why: Attribution duties stay the same whether or not AI helped ("regardless of whether AI assisted"), so the user owns attribution: P29; P24 would imply an AI disclosure that is not what is said.
units.anchor: Where attribution is expected, provide it

units.why: Says AI-produced fabrication, falsification or plagiarism is research misconduct and users answer for it ("responsible for the integrity of anything you propose... submit"). It is a research rule, P62.
units.anchor: whether produced by you or by an AI tool you used, can constitute research misconduct

units.why: Asks users to "do your research on the tools" and understand data retention and training before choosing, i.e. evaluate a tool: P117.
units.anchor: understand how it handles your data

units.why: Tells users to "check back as guidance evolves", a duty to stay current: P102.
units.anchor: check back as guidance evolves alongside the technology

units.why: Points readers to ai.usu.edu as the "authoritative sources" and says to refer to them: P115 pointer to further guidance.
units.anchor: are the authoritative sources for USU procedures, approved tools

units.why: Forbids buying an AI service USU already provides and points users to centrally managed tools, which is use of university-provided tools, P92.
units.anchor: Do not acquire a service that USU already provides.

units.why: Moderate-risk data may be used "only with AI tools that have appropriate institutional or contractual protections": protects data and prefers vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Use only with AI tools that have appropriate institutional or contractual protections in place.

units.why: High-risk data (FERPA, HIPAA, export-controlled): "Do not use with consumer AI tools", a data-protection ban: P50.
units.anchor: Do not use with consumer AI tools.

units.why: Says role-specific guidance, including syllabus expectations, lives on another page, so this document points elsewhere: P115. It sets no syllabus rule itself.
units.anchor: Guidance tailored to faculty, researchers, and administrative staff

units.why: Names the AI Tools page as "source of truth" for approved tools, i.e. know the approved list: P92.
units.anchor: That page is the source of truth for tool availability and approval status.

units.why: Asks users to judge appropriateness by data, purpose and law, not tool approval alone: weighing context before use, P118.
units.anchor: whether a use of AI is appropriate also depends on the data you put in
units.fit_note: Context factors are data, purpose and law, not benefits and values.

units.why: Centrally contracted services are "the approved method of acquisition": use of university-approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: that is the approved method of acquisition

units.why: Describes the data protection USU gives on tenant accounts ("opt out of... model training"), supporting vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: opt out of contributing your inputs and outputs to AI model training by default

units.why: "always verify that the specific tool you are using is appropriate" is assessing a tool's fit before use, P117.
units.anchor: always verify that the specific tool you are using is appropriate for your data

units.why: Listed under "Prohibited Uses": generating illegal content. A general conduct ban on malicious AI use, P74.
units.anchor: Generating content that is illegal under federal or state law

units.why: Bans deepfakes that "impersonate... deceive, harass, defame": P74 (deceptive or malicious AI use).
units.anchor: Creating AI-generated images, audio, or video (deepfakes) that realistically impersonate a real person

units.why: Prohibits entering export-controlled or CUI data into AI tools not reviewed for it: protecting confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: Entering data subject to export control regulations (EAR, ITAR)

units.why: Bans AI use in grant peer review ("NIH and NSF prohibit generative AI in peer review"), explicitly named in P62.
units.anchor: Uploading or submitting grant proposals or reviewer materials to any AI tool

units.why: Bans AI tools by origin of operator ("foreign adversary countries"). No type covers a country-based tool ban, so UNCOVERED; P65 is institutional vetting, not a blanket ban.
units.anchor: Using AI tools operated by entities subject to the laws of foreign adversary countries
units.uncovered_note: Prohibits use of AI tools operated by entities in listed foreign adversary countries for university work.

units.why: "sole basis for consequential decisions about individuals, including... grades, hiring... discipline" matches P73 exactly.
units.anchor: Using AI as the sole basis for consequential decisions about individuals

units.why: Bans discriminatory AI use against protected classes. P53 only names concerns about bias, and this is a rule, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Any use of AI that would discriminate against individuals on bases protected by Title VI
units.uncovered_note: Prohibits AI uses that discriminate against people on legally protected bases.

units.why: Bans emotion recognition and sensitive-trait inference about students and staff. No existing type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Using AI to infer emotional state, affect, or sensitive traits
units.uncovered_note: Prohibits using AI to infer emotional state or sensitive personal traits of students, employees or applicants.

units.why: Bans impersonation "intended to deceive": P74. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: Using AI to generate content that impersonates another individual

units.why: Bans using AI to breach security, which P74 lists ("breach security"). P126 is about securing accounts, not this.
units.anchor: Using AI tools to probe, exploit, or bypass university security measures

units.why: Limits sharing university data with AI providers for model training, as P65 describes ("limits on licensing or sharing university data").
units.anchor: Permitting USU institutional data to be used to train or fine-tune external

units.why: Institutional data may go only into tools USU approved ("Personal accounts and free-tier tools are not approved paths"): use approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: Processing any USU institutional data, regardless of classification, in AI tools that USU has not

units.why: Names the NIST AI RMF as the institution's framework for AI risk: P56 institution-wide framework.
units.anchor: informed by the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

units.why: An "inventory of approved AI services" is documentation of deployed AI systems, P98.
units.anchor: is USU's maintained inventory of centrally evaluated AI services

units.why: Names the AI Committee, InfoSec, CDPO and Office of Research as owners of oversight and review: P80.
units.anchor: The USU AI Committee provides executive oversight of AI adoption and this guidance

units.why: Sets a review cycle ("reviewed at least annually"): P54.
units.anchor: reviewed at least annually, and when contracts change or new services are evaluated

units.why: USU can revoke approved status of AI tools, which is periodic re-evaluation of approved tools as P65 now includes.
units.anchor: USU may change a tool's status or delist it if protections lapse.

units.why: Gives people affected by an AI-supported decision a path to raise concerns. P64 is for students accused of AI misuse; P71 is reporting incidents. So UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Individuals affected by an AI-supported decision may raise concerns with the responsible office
units.uncovered_note: People affected by an AI-supported decision may raise concerns with the responsible office or the CDPO.

units.why: AI services based abroad (e.g. DeepSeek) are discouraged, "discourages the use", not banned: P03.
units.anchor: USU discourages the use of such services for university work.

units.why: Use of a discouraged foreign service requires review with the governing unit first, a prior-approval step: P107.
units.anchor: you are expected to work with the relevant governing unit to evaluate it before use

units.why: Endorses department website chatbots and says IT is building them, an operational AI use: P76.
units.anchor: This is a great use of AI, and USU IT is actively working on it.

units.why: A rule specifically for AI agents (OpenClaw, Hermes): the deployer is accountable. Agents are the subject of P07.
units.anchor: As the person deploying an AI agent, you are accountable for its actions.
units.fit_note: Covers agents generally, not editors or IDEs.

units.why: Asks that agents be "sandboxed and clearly scoped", a control on AI agents named in P126.
units.anchor: ensure agents are properly sandboxed and clearly scoped

units.why: Warns against giving bots access to email, files or passwords; protecting personal data, P50.
units.anchor: do not give it access to anything sensitive

units.why: Requires extra review (PIA and security review) of any service with AI components before purchase: P65 as broadened.
units.anchor: should receive additional scrutiny during procurement, over and above the standard process

units.why: Asks staff to verify vendor protections when a vendor adds AI features: P65 review of vendors.
units.anchor: Do not assume that existing contractual protections automatically extend to AI features

units.why: Offers local models as a way to keep sensitive data in house ("sensitive workflows"): data protection, P50.
units.anchor: Local and self-hosted AI models can be a good option for sensitive workflows

documents.title: AI in Teaching: Communicate about AI
documents.stance_why: "instructors are granted some autonomy to determine their own class guidelines" and the page offers templates in categories (prohibited, permitted as directed, allowed and encouraged, plus a guidelines variant), so it sets no stance itself and delegates.
tiers: AI use permitted only as directed with specific assignments
AI use permitted under certain guidelines
documents.summary: Teaching-center page telling instructors to state AI rules in the syllabus and giving four template statements from prohibited to encouraged. USU leaves the choice to each instructor and routes enforcement through Article VI of the Student Code.

units.why: "every teacher should address the topic of acceptable AI use in their courses" asks instructors to state expectations, P09.
units.anchor: every teacher should address the topic of acceptable AI use in their courses

units.why: Instructors are expected to understand AI and its effect on their discipline before setting policy: P63 (faculty learning AI).
units.anchor: teachers should also be able to demonstrate a nuanced understanding of AI technology

units.why: "instructors are granted some autonomy to determine their own class guidelines": the rule is set per instructor, P04.
units.anchor: instructors are granted some autonomy to determine their own class guidelines relative to AI

units.why: "must be clearly defined in the syllabus" requires the syllabus AI statement, P09. Enforcement is coded separately.
units.anchor: such guidelines must be clearly defined in the syllabus

units.why: "enforcement must follow the procedures outlined in Article VI" is the formal integrity procedure, P81.
units.anchor: enforcement must follow the procedures outlined in Article VI of the student code

units.why: Lists three categories: prohibited, permitted as directed, allowed and encouraged: named categories of AI use, P05.
units.anchor: Class guidelines relative to AI typically fall into three broad categories

units.why: Suggests making the category clear to students, a communication practice beyond listing the rule; P66 closest.
units.anchor: Students may find it helpful if they can clearly identify which category
units.fit_note: Concerns clarity of category labeling rather than explaining reasons.

units.why: Supplies template statements for instructors to adapt: P110.
units.anchor: Listed below are template guideline statements that may help you draft your own course guidelines.

units.why: Template for a ban: "use of AI tools to generate content or responses for assignments is prohibited". It bans AI on assignments, so P01.
units.anchor: the use of AI tools to generate content or responses for assignments is prohibited

units.why: "may not submit work that is wholly or partially generated by AI" is the ban on AI-produced submissions, P19.
units.anchor: Students may not submit work that is wholly or partially generated by AI.

units.why: Names chatbots, image generators and coding assistants as covered tools, extending the ban to coding assistants, so P07.
units.anchor: This includes chatbots like ChatGPT and Copilot, image generators, coding assistants
units.fit_note: Lists tool categories covered; does not mention disabling editor features.

units.why: Sets a limit on grammar checkers ("should not be used in ways that greatly modify writing style"), a specific prose-tool rule: P18.
units.anchor: Tools that provide grammar checking (such as Grammarly) should not be used in ways that

units.why: Gives the reason for the ban: doing the work builds foundational skills ("by doing and presenting their own work"): P41.
units.anchor: strengthen students' foundational skills as thinkers, creators, and communicators by doing and presenting their own

units.why: Names Copyleaks detection software as a way to review submissions: P40 (tools used to identify misuse).
units.anchor: assignment submissions may be reviewed by AI detection software such as Copyleaks

units.why: Prohibited AI use may be "reported as an academic integrity violation" under Article 6: misuse is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: it may be reported as an academic integrity violation in accordance with

units.why: Notes that Article 6 gives "due process... including options for appeal" to accused students: P64.
units.anchor: outlines due process for instructors and students, including options for appeal

units.why: States concrete sanctions in advance ("a reduced grade and/or requirement to resubmit"): P37.
units.anchor: Possible sanctions may include a reduced grade and/or requirement to resubmit the assignment.

units.why: Template for permission case by case: AI "only for specific assignments". Which assignments allow AI is decided per assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: students are permitted to use AI tools only for specific assignments and according to specific

units.why: Guidelines are placed in assignment instructions ("which tools students may use and for what purposes"): P09.
units.anchor: These guidelines are detailed in the assignment instructions and describe which tools students may use

units.why: Says what applies when an assignment does not allow AI ("all other assignments"): the fallback is no AI, P06.
units.anchor: For all other assignments and tasks, students are expected to do their own work without

units.why: "responsible for the content and quality of their assignment submissions" and show "own ideas": ownership, P29.
units.anchor: Students will be responsible for the content and quality of their assignment submissions

units.why: Detection applies when AI is "not expressly allowed"; P40. Differs from the first template in scope of use.
units.anchor: In cases where AI use is not expressly allowed, submissions may be reviewed using AI

units.why: Template permitting AI "for all assignments, but only according to specific guidelines": permitted by default with conditions, P02.
units.anchor: students are permitted to use AI tools

units.why: Listed permitted purpose "Brainstorming ideas": P15. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: Brainstorming ideas

units.why: Listed permitted purpose "Researching topics"; nearest is finding sources, P104.
units.anchor: Researching topics
units.fit_note: Researching topics generally, with no source-verification condition.

units.why: "Outlining concepts" is outlining support for writing, P91.
units.anchor: Outlining concepts

units.why: "Writing feedback" from AI on one's own writing, P91.
units.anchor: Writing feedback

units.why: "Writing revision" is revising one's own writing: P91.
units.anchor: Writing revision

units.why: "Data analysis" is a listed use: P89. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: Data analysis

units.why: "Textual comparison and analysis" is analysis of material, closest to P89.
units.anchor: Textual comparison and analysis
units.fit_note: Analysis of text rather than data.

units.why: "Generating initial drafts" permits AI-written first drafts, a prose rule: P18.
units.anchor: Generating initial drafts
units.fit_note: Allows AI to produce drafts, not only treat prose separately.

units.why: "Generating graphs and images": P106. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: Generating graphs and images

units.why: "Generating starter code" lets students use AI-generated code: P16.
units.anchor: Generating starter code
units.fit_note: Permitted without stated caps; limits come only from the guidelines the instructor adds.

units.why: "Coding assistance" is permitted use of AI for code, closest to P16.
units.anchor: Coding assistance
units.fit_note: General coding help rather than generated code under stated conditions.

units.why: "Debugging code" is AI help to debug: P13.
units.anchor: Debugging code

units.why: Optional text: "AI should be cited as a reference... whenever its outputs are used": cite AI, P24.
units.anchor: AI should be cited as a reference

units.why: Asks students to ensure AI content "does not plagiarize or infringe": P120 risk of unintentional plagiarism.
units.anchor: make sure the AI content they use does not plagiarize or infringe upon the copyrights

units.why: Optional statement "with each assignment submission": P24 (disclose with submission), not P25 since no prompt/output is demanded.
units.anchor: Students are expected to include a statement with each assignment submission stating 1) which AI
units.policy: Students include a statement with each assignment submission saying which AI tools they used, for what purposes, and how they used and modified the AI's output with their own contributions.
units.fit_note: Also asks how the output was modified.

units.why: Template says AI is "permitted and encouraged": P02.
units.anchor: students are permitted and encouraged to use AI tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot

units.why: A best practice: "Thoroughly review AI output for... inaccuracies, bias": P31.
units.anchor: Thoroughly review AI output for relevance, depth, inaccuracies, bias, plagiarism

units.why: Bars using another person's likeness or voice without permission: impersonation conduct, P74.
units.anchor: Refrain from inputting or producing imagery, video, or audio of another person's likeness

units.why: Protects others' private data from AI tools: P50.
units.anchor: Refrain from submitting sensitive or private information about another person to an AI tool.

units.why: Students should not upload "copyright-protected or paywalled content": P49 (protected works into AI tools).
units.anchor: Refrain from uploading copyright-protected or paywalled content to an AI tool

units.why: Best practice in the encouraged template to cite AI whenever outputs are used: P24.
units.anchor: Cite AI as a reference whenever its outputs are used, quoted, or paraphrased.

units.why: Optional "acknowledgment statement with the submission" naming tools and purposes: P24.
units.anchor: students are expected to include an acknowledgment statement with the submission

units.why: Instructors may allow different AI help on different assignments ("varying levels of AI assistance"): per-assignment rule, P04.
units.anchor: You may find that you are comfortable allowing varying levels of AI assistance for certain

units.why: Asks instructors to put which tools, types of help, banned uses, citation and review expectations in each assignment description: P09 (assignment instructions).
units.anchor: be sure to include your expectations in your assignment descriptions
units.policy: Instructors include their AI expectations in assignment descriptions: which tools are permitted, what types of assistance, unacceptable uses and outputs, citation and acknowledgement, and critical review and accountability.

units.why: Frames instructors' own use as modeling appropriate use: P112.
units.anchor: An excellent way of promoting appropriate AI use is to model it.

units.why: Instructors should cite AI used in drafting course materials: P48.
units.anchor: If you use AI to help draft an assignment description or a paragraph in your

units.why: Instructors should tell students they use AI for grading feedback and that they review it: disclosure of instructor AI use, P47.
units.anchor: inform students that you will be using AI for that purpose and reassure them that

units.why: Instructors can demonstrate effective AI use in class: courses teach or demonstrate AI use, P44.
units.anchor: demonstrating what effective and appropriate use of AI looks like for class activities

documents.title: 2.8 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use & Compliance
documents.stance_why: "USU encourages faculty and students to use AI tools to enhance learning experiences while maintaining responsible and ethical engagement" and conditions such as not uploading sensitive data and verifying output. Allowed with conditions, no ban, so permit. Faculty are only "encouraged" to define coursework expectations.
documents.summary: Information-security policy 5200.2.8 on AI use covering data protection, verification of output, citation, and a short academic section. It encourages AI use with responsible handling and leaves syllabus rules to faculty.

units.why: "must align with university policies, security guidelines, and ethical standards": comply with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools must align with university policies, security guidelines, and ethical standards.

units.why: Bars uploading sensitive data to AI tools without a university privacy agreement: P50.
units.anchor: is not uploaded or processed in AI tools unless the university has an established privacy

units.why: Output "must be reviewed for accuracy, bias" before use in coursework: P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated content must be reviewed for accuracy, bias, and compliance with copyright regulations

units.why: AI "must not replace critical thinking": the human stays the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: must not replace critical thinking, academic rigor, or professional judgment

units.why: Sends all users to the AI Guidance page: P115.
units.anchor: should refer to USU's AI Guidance for official procedures, best practices, and available AI tools

units.why: States why the policy exists and its purpose, "clear guidelines for its responsible and ethical use": P56 preamble.
units.anchor: it is critical to establish clear guidelines for its responsible and ethical use across the

units.why: A duty to "promptly report" data exposure into AI tools: P71.
units.anchor: Promptly report concerns regarding entry of sensitive or restricted data into an AI tool

units.why: Faculty "encouraged to clearly define AI usage expectations in their syllabi" is a syllabus-statement expectation, P09; wording is softer than "must".
units.anchor: Faculty members are encouraged to clearly define AI usage expectations in their syllabi.

units.why: Directs faculty to sample syllabus statements: P110. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: Sample syllabus statements and detailed guidance on communicating AI policies can be found

units.why: Research use of AI calls for caution: P62 (research and scholarship).
units.anchor: Researchers at USU should exercise caution when integrating AI tools into their work.

units.why: Encourages AI for administrative work under data-security compliance: P76.
units.anchor: USU encourages the responsible use of AI to enhance administrative efficiency

units.why: Administrative users may not put PII into personal AI tools, and are pointed to supported tools: P50.
units.anchor: Do not upload sensitive, restricted, or personal data / personally identifiable information (PII)

units.why: Verification before use in official communications: P31, administrative context.
units.anchor: AI-generated content should be verified for accuracy and potential biases before use in official communications.

units.why: Bans sensitive data in public AI tools such as ChatGPT: P50.
units.anchor: Public AI tools should not be used to process, store, or analyze sensitive university data.

units.why: States that "AI-generated responses can be unreliable or false": P31 (output is often wrong).
units.anchor: AI-generated responses can be unreliable or false.

units.why: If AI content is used in research or coursework, "the AI tool must be properly cited": P24.
units.anchor: the AI tool must be properly cited

units.why: Names bias in training data as a concern: P53.
units.anchor: AI tools are trained on vast amounts of data, which may include biases.

units.why: Users should "critically evaluate" and correct biased output: P31.
units.anchor: should critically evaluate AI-generated content and take steps to identify and correct biased outputs

units.why: AI output may reproduce copyrighted material without attribution, a plagiarism risk: P120.
units.anchor: AI-generated content may include copyrighted material without proper attribution

units.why: AI must not replace peer-reviewed research or professional advice; closest is P32 (AI does not replace human thinking).
units.anchor: AI should never be used as a substitute for peer-reviewed research or professional recommendations.
units.fit_note: About not substituting AI for scholarly sources and expert advice, not for the student's own thinking.

units.why: AI use must follow existing academic integrity policies ("must adhere to USU's academic integrity policies"): P77.
units.anchor: Faculty and students must adhere to USU's academic integrity policies when utilizing AI in coursework

units.why: "USU encourages faculty and students to use AI tools": AI is welcomed, P02.
units.anchor: USU encourages faculty and students to use AI tools to enhance learning experiences

units.why: Names benefits of AI without a rule: P87.
units.anchor: AI offers significant opportunities to enhance learning, research, and operations at USU.

units.why: "encouraged to stay informed" about AI: P102. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: are encouraged to stay informed

units.why: Encourages "officially supported AI tools": P92. It is a listed item the template permits, so the type is the nearest permitted-use type.
units.anchor: utilize officially supported AI tools
